I farm 10.1 mu here in Quzhou. Most of my land — about 8 mu — I do wheat-maize double crop like everyone around me. That is the way here. The other 2 mu I keep for spring potato because it brings in more cash and my wife and I can manage it by hand. My children work in town so it is mostly me and my wife in the field, with some hired help at wheat harvest.

For winter wheat, I plant improved seed — I buy Jimai variety from the same dealer as my neighbor Lao Wang, he got 520 kg last year. I put down compound fertilizer 15-15-15 as base, about 50 kg/mu, then topdress urea at jointing, maybe 20 kg/mu. That comes to around 26 kg N, 7-8 kg P, 7-8 kg K. I know some say less is enough but if the wheat is yellow in spring I lose too much. Better to add a little extra. I irrigate before winter, then at jointing, at heading, and once at grain filling — four times from the well. Spray two or three times for aphids and rust. Plough after the maize stalks are chopped.

For summer maize I use hybrid seed, Zhengdan or similar. After wheat harvest I go straight no-till with the planter. I put compound as base about 40 kg/mu and topdress urea at big trumpet stage 15 kg/mu. Maize does not need as much P and K as wheat if I already fertilized well. Irrigate twice usually — after sowing and at tasseling. One or two sprays for borer and armyworm.

For spring potato I plant improved seed potatoes. Potato eats a lot of potassium so I use more compound and add potassium sulfate. I plough deep before planting. Irrigate three or four times and spray for late blight three times — potato disease is the thing that ruins you.
